title: Disjunction
summary: Disjunction joins alternatives and says that at least one is admitted under the chosen logic.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared propositional language context is fixed.

content.plain: Disjunction joins alternatives and says that at least one is admitted under the chosen logic.
content.exact: P∨Q is true in classical semantics exactly when at least one of P or Q is true; constructive proof normally supplies which side holds and its proof.
content.example: ‘n is negative or n is nonnegative’ is a disjunction over an ordered number system.
content.caveat: Inclusive mathematical disjunction differs from everyday exclusive ‘or’, and its proof meaning varies by logic.
